intro: Sulechów, a small town in Lubusz on Poland's western edge, holds two argued-over pines in the same state forest. Sosna Waligóra, a kilometre and a half out on an 18-stop trail, is fatter at chest height than at the ground, evidence it started life as two trees fused into one. Ten kilometres further into the same forest district stands Sosna Rzepicha, thicker still and the country's current record holder, though nobody has published its age and reaching it means leaving the trail.
meta_description: Sulechów, Poland: two record pines, one forest district. Waligóra (620cm, fused trunk, marked trail) and Rzepicha, Poland's current thickest pine.
question_meta: Sulechów holds two record pines. The one with a documented age is Sosna Waligóra, roughly 160 to 170 years old.
question_answer: Sosna Waligóra, a Scots pine in state forest east of town, generally reckoned 160 to 170 years old. Its neighbour Rzepicha, ten kilometres into the same forest district, is thicker and holds the national thickest-pine title under the current measuring method, but no source publishes an age for it, so Waligóra remains the tree with a documented age.
question_context: Waligóra is fatter higher up than at the base, 620 centimetres round at 1.3 metres against 527 at ground level, which is not how a single trunk normally grows. The likeliest explanation is that at least two young pines grew together low down and fused, with the combined mass then forking at about two metres into eight bent limbs, now held together with steel cables. That shape, rather than age, is what makes it so thick: at only about 160 to 170 years old it is younger than its bulk suggests. It has been protected since December 1982, reconfirmed by the voivode in 2006. An 18-stop educational trail called Do Waligóry has run 3.4 kilometres out to the tree since 1998, with a parking area just off national road 32. Its neighbour Rzepicha, five trunks fused into one crown, measures 568 centimetres round and is the country's thickest Scots pine under current measuring rules, having taken the title from Waligóra when the method changed rather than by growing past it. No age has been published for Rzepicha anywhere found, and it has no trail or parking, only a walk off-path through wet ground. If you know its age, tell us.

faq.q: What is special about these trees?
faq.a: Waligóra is fatter at chest height than at the ground, evidence it began as two pines fused low down rather than one. Rzepicha, ten kilometres away in the same forest, is five trunks fused into a single crown and is Poland's current record holder for thickest Scots pine.
Waligóra is roughly 160 to 170 years old, young for a tree of this bulk since its thickness comes from its fused shape rather than its age. No age has been published for Rzepicha.
Yes, both stand in open state forest with no fee. Waligóra has a parking area and a signed trail; Rzepicha does not.

Waligóra stands about 80 metres off national road 32, 1.5km east of Sulechów, with an 18-stop trail leading to it. Rzepicha is 10.5km further into the same forest district, near Górki Małe and Pomorsko, reached on foot off-path through wet ground with no marked trail or parking.

faq.q: Which one is really the thickest pine in Poland?
faq.a: Rzepicha, at 568cm, under the current measuring method. Waligóra held the national title under the older method and remains the easier tree to actually visit.

trees.name: Sosna Waligóra

location.address: Leśnictwo Klępsk, Nadleśnictwo Sulechów, beside national road 32, about 1.5 km east of Sulechów

trees.story:
This pine is fatter at chest height than it is at the ground, which is not how trees are meant to work. At 1.3 metres it measures 620 centimetres round. At the base it measures 527. The likeliest explanation is that Waligóra was never one tree: at least two grew together low down, fused into a single mass, and the whole thing divides at about two metres into eight bent limbs.

That accident of biography makes it the second thickest pine in Poland. The thickest, Rzepicha, happens to stand in the same forest district. In a national competition in 2002, Waligóra was judged the thickest specimen anyone put forward.

The age is the surprise in the other direction. It is only about 160 to 170 years old, young for a tree with a reputation, and its bulk comes from its shape rather than from time. The eight limbs are now held with steel cables and there is a low wooden fence around the base.

It is easy to reach and hard to miss: 80 metres off national road 32, a kilometre and a half east of Sulechów, with a parking area at the roadside. An 18-stop educational trail called Do Waligóra has run 3.4 kilometres out to it since 1998, and the local green and black hiking routes pass the same way. Protected since December 1982, reconfirmed by the voivode in 2006, and stranger up close than any photograph makes it look.
trees.access: Free, publicly accessible. Stands in state forest (Nadleśnictwo Sulechów) about 80 m off national road 32, with a roadside parking area and a 3.4 km, 18-stop educational trail ('Do Waligóry', laid out 1998) leading to it; also on the green and black marked hiking trails of gmina Sulechów.
trees.transport: About 1.5 km east of Sulechów on national road 32; no direct public transport to the tree itself, reached by car (parking on site) or on foot/bike from Sulechów via the marked trail.

trees.name: Sosna Rzepicha

location.address: Nowy Świat forestry district, Nadleśnictwo Sulechów, between the villages of Pomorsko and Górki Małe, Lubusz Voivodeship

trees.story: Poland's thickest Scots pine took the title from a tree ten kilometres up the road, and it never had to grow to do it. The measuring rules changed. Sosna Waligóra held the record under the older method; Rzepicha holds it under the current one, at 5.68 metres round. The figure makes more sense once you see the trunk, which is five stems fused into a single mass, carrying one wide, well-built crown 27 metres up. There are dead branches in it with scars where the wounds closed over, and it is otherwise rated in very good health. It has been a protected nature monument since 1996, in the Nowy Świat forestry district between Pomorsko and Górki Małe, about ten and a half kilometres from Sulechów. Reaching it is the hard part, and it is worth being plain about that. Waligóra has a marked trail and somewhere to leave the car. Rzepicha has neither. It stands at the edge of a thicket on the Oder floodplain, beside a pool, with marshy meadow in front of it, and the last stretch from Górki Małe or Pomorsko is off the path and through wet ground. Wear boots. Nobody has published an age for this pine, which for a tree of its size is unusual. If you know of a count or a dated record, tell us.
trees.access: Free in principle (state forest), but genuinely hard to reach: no direct road, stands at the edge of a thicket and marshy meadow on the Oder floodplain terrace near a pool. Unlike its neighbour Sosna Waligóra (sul_001), which has a marked trail and roadside parking, Rzepicha requires walking off-trail through wet ground.
trees.transport: About 10.5km from Sulechów town centre and from the Sosna Waligóra site (sul_001), in the same forest district. No public transport; reached on foot from Górki Małe or Pomorsko.
